question_en: Your friend suddenly says, “I’m getting married tomorrow.”
choice_labels: 헐 (Heol) → A stunned reaction like “What…?” when you freeze from sudden shock.
설마 (Seol-ma) → Used when you doubt something.

question_en: You take one bite of food and it’s unbelievably delicious.
question_kr: 음식을 한 입 먹었는데 충격적으로 맛있다.
choice_labels: 대박 (Dae-bak) → “Amazing!” used when something is impressively good.
헐 (Heol) → Shock, but not mainly positive praise.

question_en: Your friend tells you something hard to believe, so you check again.
question_kr: 친구가 믿기 어려운 말을 해서 다시 확인한다.
choice_labels: 진짜 (Jin-jja) → “Really?” used to confirm surprising information.

question_en: Your friend says they won the lottery.
choice_labels: 설마 (Seol-ma) → “No way…” used when you strongly doubt something.

question_en: Your friend is three hours late and acts like it’s nothing.
choice_labels: 어이없어 (Eo-i-eopseo) → “This is absurd” when something feels unfair or ridiculous.

question_en: Your friend suggests a plan and you casually agree.
question_kr: 친구가 계획을 말하고 당신은 가볍게 동의한다.
choice_labels: 응응 (Eung-eung) → Casual “yeah / uh-huh” used for light agreement.

question_en: Someone says something unbelievable and you strongly deny it.
question_kr: 누군가 말도 안 되는 이야기를 해서 강하게 부정한다.

question_en: Your friend suggests meeting at a specific time and you accept confidently.
question_kr: 친구가 약속 시간을 제안하고 당신은 확실하게 수락한다.
choice_labels: 오케이 (O-ke-i) → “Okay / Deal” used for clear agreement.

question_en: Someone helps you fix something.
choice_labels: 고마워 (Go-ma-wo) → “Thank you” used to express gratitude.

question_en: Your friend tells you they passed an important exam.
Your friend suddenly says, “I quit my job today.”
question_kr: 친구가 갑자기 “나 오늘 회사 그만뒀어”라고 말한다.
choice_labels: 헐 진짜? (Heol jin-jja?) → A reaction that starts with shock (“헐”) and immediately moves to confirmation (“Really?”).
와 대박이다 (Wa dae-bak-i-da) → Used for strong positive excitement.
진짜야? (Jin-jja-ya?) → Used for focused confirmation without shock.
설마 그게 돼? (Seol-ma geu-ge dwae?) → Used for disbelief, not confirmation.

question_en: You check your phone and see a huge bonus amount.
question_kr: 폰으로 보너스 금액을 확인했는데 엄청 크다.
choice_labels: 와 대박이다 (Wa dae-bak-i-da) → “Wow, this is amazing!” used for high-energy excitement.
헐 진짜? (Heol jin-jja?) → Shock + confirm, not pure excitement.
설마 그게 돼? (Seol-ma geu-ge dwae?) → Doubt.

question_en: Your friend tells you something hard to believe, so you focus and check.
question_kr: 친구가 믿기 어려운 말을 해서 집중해서 확인한다.
choice_labels: 진짜야? (Jin-jja-ya?) → “Really?” used for focused confirmation without shock.
헐 진짜? (Heol jin-jja?) → Shock comes first, not here.
설마 그게 돼? (Seol-ma geu-ge dwae?) → Doubt, not neutral confirmation.

question_en: Your friend says they finished everything in one day.
question_kr: 친구가 하루 만에 모든 걸 끝냈다고 말한다.
choice_labels: 설마 그게 돼? (Seol-ma geu-ge dwae?) → “No way…” used for strong disbelief.

question_en: Your friend blames you for something that was clearly their mistake.
question_kr: 본인 실수인데 오히려 당신에게 책임을 돌린다.
choice_labels: 진짜 어이없다 (Jin-jja eo-i-eop-da) → “This is seriously ridiculous” expressing absurdity with evaluation.
설마 그게 돼? (Seol-ma geu-ge dwae?) → Doubt.

question_en: Your friend tells you an unbelievably high price.
choice_labels: 말도 안 돼 (Mal-do an-dwae) → “That makes no sense” used for strong denial.
설마 그게 돼? (Seol-ma geu-ge dwae?) → Doubt, not rejection.

question_en: Your friend shows you an unbelievable result.
question_kr: 친구가 말도 안 되는 결과를 보여준다.
choice_labels: 미쳤다 (Mi-chyeot-da) → “That’s crazy (in a good way)” used for positive shock.
설마 그게 돼? (Seol-ma geu-ge dwae?) → Doubt.

question_en: You watch a video and slowly start laughing harder and harder.
choice_labels: 너무 웃겨 (Neo-mu ut-gyeo) → “This is so funny” used when laughter builds up.
설마 그게 돼? (Seol-ma geu-ge dwae?) → Doubt.

question_en: You hear your friend’s point and completely agree.
choice_labels: 나도 인정 (Na-do in-jeong) → “I agree / I admit it” used with respect.

question_en: Your friend is late and you want them to hurry.
question_kr: 친구가 계속 늦고 있어서 빨리 오라고 한다.
choice_labels: 빨리 와 (Ppal-li wa) → “Come quickly” used to push action.

question_en: Your friend shows you a travel plan on their phone.
choice_labels: 완전 좋아 (Wan-jeon jo-a) → “I really like it” used for clear, confirmed satisfaction.
대박 (Dae-bak) → Strong excitement, not calm approval.

question_en: You see a puppy acting cute.
choice_labels: 너무 귀엽다 (Neo-mu gwi-yeop-da) → “So cute” used with soft, warm emotion.

question_en: You hear a strange noise in a quiet night.
choice_labels: 좀 무섭다 (Jom mu-seop-da) → “A bit scary” used for low-level fear.

question_en: You watch a very touching scene.
choice_labels: 눈물 나 (Nun-mul na) → “It makes me tear up” used for emotional build-up.
슬프다 (Seul-peu-da) → Just sad, not emotional build.

question_en: Right before starting something important, you raise the energy.
choice_labels: 가보자 (Ga-bo-ja) → “Let’s go” used to push energy forward.

question_en: Your friend shows you something they made alone, and it's amazing.
question_kr: 친구가 혼자 만든 결과물을 보여주는데 압도적이다.
choice_labels: 미쳤다 이건 (Mi-chyeot-da i-geon) → “This is insane” used with awe and object-focused evaluation.
이거 레전드다 (I-geo re-jeon-deu-da) → Higher hype tone.

question_en: Your friend is going too far joking about someone.
choice_labels: 와 이건 좀 심하다 (Wa i-geon jom sim-ha-da) → “That’s too much” used for moral judgment.
말도 안 돼 (Mal-do an-dwae) → Logical denial.

question_en: Your friend crosses the line with what they say.
choice_labels: 그건 좀 아니지 (Geu-geon jom a-ni-ji) → “That’s not okay” used to set a boundary calmly.
와 이건 좀 심하다 (Wa i-geon jom sim-ha-da) → Judgment, not boundary.

question_en: Your friend performs something incredibly impressive.
choice_labels: 이거 레전드다 (I-geo re-jeon-deu-da) → “This is legendary” used for top-level praise.
미쳤다 이건 (Mi-chyeot-da i-geon) → Awe + object focus.
완전 좋아 (Wan-jeon jo-a) → Satisfaction, not hype.

question_en: You hear something that makes no logical sense at all.
question_kr: 상식적으로 말이 안 되는 이야기를 듣는다.
choice_labels: 진짜 말도 안 돼 (Jin-jja mal-do an-dwae) → “This seriously makes no sense” used for strong judgment.

question_en: You find something that perfectly matches your taste.
choice_labels: 완전 내 스타일이야 (Wan-jeon nae seu-ta-il-i-ya) → “This is totally my style” used for taste alignment.

question_en: You see a result that exceeds expectations and acknowledge it.
choice_labels: 이건 인정이다 (I-geon in-jeong-i-da) → “I have to admit this” used for clear recognition.
나도 인정 (Na-do in-jeong) → Agreement, not evaluation.

question_en: Things keep not working and frustration builds up.
question_kr: 상황이 계속 안 풀려 답답함이 쌓인다.
choice_labels: 너무 답답하다 (Neo-mu dap-dap-ha-da) → “This is so frustrating” used for built-up tension.

question_en: The same mistake keeps happening and it annoys you.
choice_labels: 진짜 짜증난다 (Jin-jja jja-jeung-nan-da) → “This is really annoying” used for irritation peak.

question_en: You expected something to be bad, but it's actually okay.
choice_labels: 생각보다 괜찮은데? (Saeng-gak-bo-da gwaen-chan-eun-de?) → “Better than I expected” used for re-evaluation.

question_en: Something turns out to be way more fun than expected.
choice_labels: 완전 꿀잼이다 (Wan-jeon kkul-jaem-i-da) → “This is super fun” used for high-level enjoyment evaluation.

question_en: You expected something to be fun, but it’s boring.
choice_labels: 이건 노잼이다 (I-geon no-jaem-i-da) → “This is not fun” used for low enjoyment judgment.

question_en: You experience a strange, unexplainable moment.
choice_labels: 진짜 소름 돋는다 (Jin-jja so-reum dot-neun-da) → “This gives me chills” used for awe-type reaction.

question_en: Your friend gets a great opportunity and you feel happy but envious.
choice_labels: 너무 부럽다 (Neo-mu bu-reop-da) → “I’m so jealous (in a good way)” used for positive envy.

question_en: Something is funny but also a bit sad at the same time.
choice_labels: 이건 좀 웃프다 (I-geon jom ut-peu-da) → “This is funny but sad” used for mixed emotion.

question_en: During a conversation, one comment suddenly makes the atmosphere awkward.
question_kr: 대화 중 한마디로 분위기가 갑자기 싸해진다.
choice_labels: 분위기 갑자기 싸해졌다 (Bun-wi-gi gap-ja-gi ssa-hae-jyeot-da) → “The mood suddenly turned cold” used to notice a shift in atmosphere.

question_en: You see two things that match perfectly together.
choice_labels: 이거 완전 찰떡이다 (I-geo wan-jeon chal-tteok-i-da) → “This is a perfect match” used for ideal combination.

question_en: You see a sweet couple moment.
choice_labels: 너무 달달하다 (Neo-mu dal-dal-ha-da) → “So sweet” used for relationship-based emotion.
너무 귀엽다 (Neo-mu gwi-yeop-da) → Cute, not relational.

question_en: You feel quiet sympathy for a bittersweet situation.
choice_labels: 마음이 좀 짠하다 (Ma-eum-i jom jjan-ha-da) → “It feels bittersweet” used for quiet empathy.

question_en: Someone clearly crosses the line.
choice_labels: 선 넘었다 (Seon neo-meot-da) → “That crossed the line” used for final boundary judgment.
그건 좀 아니지 (Geu-geon jom a-ni-ji) → Softer boundary.
와 이건 좀 심하다 (Wa i-geon jom sim-ha-da) → Moral judgment.

question_en: You hear something that makes no sense at all and react strongly.
question_kr: 상식적으로 납득이 안 되는 이야기를 듣는다.
correct: 야 이건 진짜 말도 안 된다
choices: 야 이건 진짜 말도 안 된다
choice_labels: 야 이건 진짜 말도 안 된다 (Ya i-geon jin-jja mal-do an-dwae-da) → “Hey, this seriously makes no sense” used for strong opinion.
말도 안 돼 (Mal-do an-dwae) → Basic denial.
진짜 말도 안 돼 (Jin-jja mal-do an-dwae) → Strong denial, less conversational.

question_en: You hear something unexpected and react honestly.
question_kr: 예상 못한 사실을 듣고 솔직하게 반응한다.
choice_labels: 솔직히 좀 충격인데? (Sol-jik-hi jom chung-gyeok-in-de?) → “Honestly, that’s kind of shocking” used for honest reaction.

question_en: You point out someone's behavior calmly but firmly.
choice_labels: 아니 이건 너무한 거 아니야? (A-ni i-geon neo-mu-han geo a-ni-ya?) → “Isn’t that too much?” used for calm authority.
그건 좀 아니지 (Geu-geon jom a-ni-ji) → Boundary.
와 이건 좀 심하다 (Wa i-geon jom sim-ha-da) → Judgment.

question_en: You acknowledge someone’s skill respectfully.
choice_labels: 이건 인정이다 (I-geon in-jeong-i-da) → “I have to admit this” used for respectful recognition.

question_en: You notice something unexpectedly funny and share it.
choice_labels: 이건 좀 웃긴데? (I-geon jom ut-gin-de?) → “That’s kind of funny” used to share light humor.

question_en: You and your friend watch something amazing together and react at the same time.
question_kr: 둘이 함께 본 장면이 너무 압도적이다.
choice_labels: 와 이건 진짜 레전드다 (Wa i-geon jin-jja re-jeon-deu-da) → “Wow, this is truly legendary” used for shared awe.
이거 레전드다 (I-geo re-jeon-deu-da) → Strong praise, but not shared.

question_en: Your friend says something so absurd you almost laugh.
question_kr: 상대 말이 너무 황당해서 웃음이 나오기 직전이다.
choice_labels: 너 지금 장난하는 거지? (Neo ji-geum jang-nan-ha-neun geo-ji?) → “You’re kidding, right?” used for absurd but playful disbelief.
말도 안 돼 (Mal-do an-dwae) → Strong denial.

question_en: You saw something amazing and share your feeling with someone.
choice_labels: 나 이거 보고 소름 돋았어 (Na i-geo bo-go so-reum do-dat-eo) → “I got chills watching this” used for personal experience sharing.
진짜 소름 돋는다 (Jin-jja so-reum dot-neun-da) → Immediate reaction.

question_en: You didn’t expect much, but it turned out okay, so you share your opinion.
question_kr: 기대 안 했는데 괜찮아서 의견을 전달한다.
choice_labels: 이건 좀 생각보다 괜찮다 (I-geon jom saeng-gak-bo-da gwaen-chan-ta) → “This is better than expected” used for re-evaluation sharing.
생각보다 괜찮은데? (Saeng-gak-bo-da gwaen-chan-eun-de?) → More internal reaction.

question_en: Someone says something that hurts you, so you express it calmly.
choice_labels: 솔직히 기분 좀 상했어 (Sol-jik-hi gi-bun jom sang-haet-eo) → “Honestly, that hurt my feelings” used for calm emotional delivery.
기분 나쁘다 (Gi-bun na-ppeu-da) → Strong and blunt.

question_en: You decide that something cannot just be ignored.
question_kr: 그냥 넘어가면 안 되는 상황이라고 판단한다.
choice_labels: 이건 그냥 넘어가기 어렵다 (I-geon geu-nyang neo-meo-ga-gi eo-ryeop-da) → “This is hard to just let go” used for firm stance.
그건 좀 아니지 (Geu-geon jom a-ni-ji) → Boundary.
와 이건 좀 심하다 (Wa i-geon jom sim-ha-da) → Judgment.

question_en: A frustrating situation finally gets resolved.
choice_labels: 와 속이 다 시원하다 (Wa sok-i da si-won-ha-da) → “I feel so relieved” used for emotional release.

question_en: You are so frustrated that you physically can't keep watching.
question_kr: 답답함이 극에 달해 더 못 보겠다.
choice_labels: 너무 답답해서 못 보겠다 (Neo-mu dap-dap-hae-seo mot bo-get-da) → “I can’t watch this anymore” due to overload.

question_en: The mood suddenly becomes awkward and you react to it.
choice_labels: 이 분위기 갑자기 왜 이래? (I bun-wi-gi gap-ja-gi wae i-rae?) → “Why did it suddenly get awkward?” used to question mood shift.

question_en: You suddenly realize reality and feel mentally drained.
choice_labels: 나 지금 현타 왔어 (Na ji-geum hyeon-ta wat-eo) → “I’m having a reality check” used for mental collapse.

question_en: You see something overly emotional and feel a bit embarrassed in a cute way.
choice_labels: 이건 좀 오글거린다 (I-geon jom o-geul-geo-rin-da) → “This is a bit cringey” used for cute, light embarrassment.

question_en: You watch something emotional together and share the feeling.
choice_labels: 와 진짜 눈물 난다 (Wa jin-jja nun-mul nan-da) → “Wow, this makes me tear up” used for shared emotion.

question_en: You find something that matches your taste and share it with someone.
choice_labels: 이거 완전 내 취향이다 (I-geo wan-jeon nae chwi-hyang-i-da) → “This is totally my taste” used for shared preference.
완전 내 스타일이야 (Wan-jeon nae seu-ta-il-i-ya) → Personal statement.

question_en: Someone achieves something impressive and you acknowledge it with respect.
choice_labels: 너 진짜 대단하다 (Neo jin-jja dae-dan-ha-da) → “You’re really amazing” used with deep respect.

question_en: You feel something is unfair and express it.
choice_labels: 이건 좀 억울한데? (I-geon jom eok-ul-han-de?) → “This feels unfair” used for expressing injustice.

question_en: Someone asks you to apologize and you question it logically.
choice_labels: 아니 왜 내가 미안해야 돼? (A-ni wae nae-ga mi-an-hae-ya dwae?) → “Why should I apologize?” used as a calm logical question.
그건 좀 아니지 (Geu-geon jom a-ni-ji) → Boundary.

question_en: Someone asks too much and you push back gently.
choice_labels: 이건 좀 무리 아니야? (I-geon jom mu-ri a-ni-ya?) → “Isn’t that too much?” used for soft limit setting.
그건 좀 아니지 (Geu-geon jom a-ni-ji) → Boundary.

question_en: You see something that exceeds expectations and react.
choice_labels: 와 이건 상상 이상이다 (Wa i-geon sang-sang i-sang-i-da) → “This is beyond imagination” used for high evaluation.

question_en: You see something valuable and decide to learn it.
choice_labels: 이건 진짜 배워야겠다 (I-geon jin-jja bae-wo-ya-get-da) → “I should really learn this” used for action decision.

question_en: You finally understand something after struggling.
choice_labels: 이제야 감 잡았다 (I-je-ya gam jap-at-da) → “Now I finally get it” used for eureka moment.

question_en: You disagree with someone's opinion but avoid direct conflict.
question_kr: 상대 의견이 납득되지 않지만 정면 충돌은 피한다.
choice_labels: 솔직히 이해는 안 된다 (Sol-jik-hi i-hae-neun an doen-da) → “Honestly, I don’t understand” used for calm disagreement.
말도 안 돼 (Mal-do an-dwae) → Strong denial.
그건 좀 아니지 (Geu-geon jom a-ni-ji) → Boundary.

question_en: You partially agree but leave room without fully committing.
choice_labels: 그럴 수도 있긴 한데… (Geu-reol su-do it-gin han-de…) → “That could be true, but…” used to hold distance.
아닌 것 같다 (A-nin geot gat-da) → More direct disagreement.

question_en: You need to reject a suggestion politely.
choice_labels: 음… 이건 아닌 것 같다 (Eum… i-geon a-nin geot gat-da) → “Hmm… I don’t think this is right” used for soft refusal.

question_en: You accept the logic but feel emotionally uncomfortable.
choice_labels: 말은 맞는데 기분은 별로다 (Mal-eun mat-neun-de gi-bun-eun byeol-lo-da) → “You’re right, but I don’t feel good about it” used for logic vs emotion.
그건 좀 아니지 (Geu-geon jom a-ni-ji) → Boundary.

question_en: Someone crosses a line, and you point it out calmly.
correct: 이건 좀 선 넘은 것 같다
choices: 이건 좀 선 넘은 것 같다
choice_labels: 이건 좀 선 넘은 것 같다 (I-geon jom seon neo-meon geot gat-da) → “I think that crossed the line” used for soft boundary.
그건 좀 아니지 (Geu-geon jom a-ni-ji) → Boundary.
와 이건 좀 심하다 (Wa i-geon jom sim-ha-da) → Moral judgment.

question_en: Something isn’t bad, but you’re unsure about it.
choice_labels: 나쁘진 않은데 애매하다 (Na-ppeu-jin an-eun-de ae-mae-ha-da) → “It’s not bad, but it’s unclear” used for neutral ambiguity.

question_en: You understand someone’s good intention but feel uncomfortable.
choice_labels: 좋은 뜻인 건 알겠는데 부담스럽다 (Jo-eun tteus-in geon al-get-neun-de bu-dam-seu-reop-da) → “I know you mean well, but it’s a bit much” used for polite discomfort.

question_en: Something starts funny but slowly becomes uncomfortable.
choice_labels: 웃기긴 한데 좀 불편하다 (Ut-gi-gin han-de jom bul-pyeon-ha-da) → “It’s funny, but also uncomfortable” used for slow mood shift.

question_en: You think someone didn’t mean harm and soften the situation.
question_kr: 상대가 일부러 그런 건 아닐 수 있다고 본다.
correct: 일부러 그런 건 아닌 것 같다
choices: 일부러 그런 건 아닌 것 같다
choice_labels: 일부러 그런 건 아닌 것 같다 (Il-bu-reo geu-reon geon a-nin geot gat-da) → “I don’t think they meant it” used to soften intent.
그건 좀 아니지 (Geu-geon jom a-ni-ji) → Boundary.

question_en: You decide it's better not to bring something up in the current situation.
question_kr: 지금은 그냥 넘어가는 게 낫다고 판단한다.
choice_labels: 분위기상 그냥 넘어가는 게 낫다 (Bun-wi-gi-sang geu-nyang neo-meo-ga-neun ge nat-da) → “Given the situation, it’s better to let it go” used for social strategy.

question_en: You decide it's better to stay quiet to avoid making things worse.
question_kr: 지금 말하면 상황이 더 나빠질 것 같다고 판단한다.
choice_labels: 지금은 말 아끼는 게 좋겠다 (Ji-geum-eun mal a-kki-neun ge jot-get-da) → “It’s better to hold back right now” used for strategic silence.

question_en: You feel someone truly deserves to be congratulated.
choice_labels: 이건 진심으로 축하해줘야 한다 (I-geon jin-sim-eu-ro chuk-ha-hae-jwo-ya han-da) → “This really deserves congratulations” used as social norm.

question_en: Someone says they're fine, but you think they might be hurt inside.
